definitions.explanation: Speaking or expressing one's thoughts honestly and directly, without evasion or pretense.

examples.japanese: {率直|そっちょく}に{言|い}うと、{賛成|さんせい}できない。
{率直|そっちょく}な{意見|いけん}をお{聞|き}かせください。
{彼|かれ}は{率直|そっちょく}に{自分|じぶん}の{間違|まちが}いを{認|みと}めた。
examples.english: He candidly admitted his own mistake.

notes:
The adverbial form of the na-adjective {率直|そっちょく}. Used when someone speaks or acts with honest directness. Often appears in the set phrase {率直|そっちょく}に{言|い}うと (frankly speaking), which serves as a softener before stating a potentially unwelcome opinion.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {率直|そっちょく}に{言|い}う: to speak frankly
- {率直|そっちょく}な{意見|いけん}: a candid opinion
- {率直|そっちょく}な{感想|かんそう}: honest impressions
- {率直|そっちょく}に{認|みと}める: to candidly admit

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {正直|しょうじき}に: honestly — more colloquial, emphasizes truthfulness rather than directness
- {素直|すなお}に: obediently, straightforwardly — implies willing compliance or naturalness, not bluntness
- あからさまに: openly, bluntly — stronger and often implies being inappropriately direct or revealing
